analysis.title: Americas Payment Technology: Consumer Spending Update: October - Fiserv SMB spend stable with improving transaction trends
key_insights: Fiserv Small Business Index sales growth rose to 2.3% YoY seasonally adjusted (SA) in October from 2.2% in September. Non-seasonally adjusted (NSA) growth fell to 1.3% from 2.4%.
SMB transactions declined 1.3% YoY in October versus -2.0% in September, the strongest transaction trend since February. Average ticket growth slowed to 3.6% YoY from 4.3%.
Essentials spend growth (2.7% YoY) outpaced Discretionary (2.0% YoY) in October. In September the split was 2.4% Essentials and 2.0% Discretionary.
SMB retail growth slowed to 1.9% YoY from 3.0% in September as back-to-school and Labor Day timing effects lapsed. Pricing growth was -0.3% and foot traffic growth was 2.2%.
Gasoline stations and fuel dealers grew 23.2% YoY and remain a meaningful contributor to headline growth. GS notes growth is somewhat concentrated in more volatile categories.
SMB restaurant spending (food services and drinking places) improved to -0.5% YoY from -1.0% in September. Transaction declines moderated to -2.7% from -3.9% while average ticket growth slowed.
Restaurant performance is bifurcated by format. Drinking places grew 3.7% YoY and full-service restaurants 0.5%, while limited-service restaurants fell 2.2%.

GS sees October SMB spending as healthy and consistent with Visa and Mastercard commentary of resilient consumer spending through October. It views the trends as supportive for payment providers with broad merchant exposure (FISV/GPN/XYZ).
GS says continued essentials strength is supportive for CHYM given its portfolio skew toward non-discretionary, everyday spend.

For restaurant-exposed names (TOST/FOUR/XYZ) GS marks the read-through negative to neutral. It calls the traffic improvement encouraging but notes restaurant spending remains below broader SMB trends.

market_movers.rationale: GS marks the October SMB data a positive read-through for horizontal payment providers with broad merchant-category exposure. Retail spending stayed healthy at 1.9% YoY.
Same positive read-through as FISV and XYZ on resilient SMB retail spending and broad category exposure.
Listed in the positive horizontal-provider read-through and in the mixed restaurant read-through (TOST/FOUR/XYZ marked -/=).
Restaurant spending improved sequentially to -0.5% YoY but stayed soft, with traffic still declining. GS marks the read-through as negative to neutral.
Restaurant spending remains below broader SMB trends despite sequential traffic improvement. GS marks the read-through as negative to neutral.
Continued strength in essentials spend is supportive given the portfolio's skew toward non-discretionary, everyday spend.

sector_views.rationale: Broad exposure across merchant categories and resilient consumer spending trends. GS states no formal rating change.
Sequential traffic improvement is encouraging, but restaurant spending remains soft and below broader SMB trends.

earnings_insights: GS notes Visa (V) and Mastercard (MA) both highlighted resilient consumer spending trends through October during their earnings. No EPS or revenue figures are cited in this report.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fiserv SMB transaction growth, all sectors (SA)
macro_indicators.interpretation: Transaction declines narrowed to the strongest level since February.
Ticket growth slowed, so the headline was supported more by transaction improvement than by pricing.
Discretionary spending was flat versus September.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fiserv SMB restaurant (food services and drinking places) spending

risk_factors: Headline growth is supported by gasoline (23.2% YoY) and growth is somewhat concentrated in more volatile categories.
Discretionary spend growth was flat at 2.0% YoY.
Restaurant spending remains pressured by declining traffic and sits below broader SMB trends.
Retail growth decelerated to 1.9% YoY from 3.0% as September timing effects lapsed.

tension_points.bull_case: SMB sales growth of 2.3% SA is steady, transaction trends are the strongest since February, and essentials are accelerating at 2.7% YoY. Visa and Mastercard also cited resilient spending through October.
tension_points.bear_case: Headline growth leans on volatile categories, with gas up 23.2% YoY. Discretionary growth is flat at 2.0%, retail slowed to 1.9% from 3.0%, and restaurant traffic is still declining.

theme_stances.key_argument: October SMB sales growth stayed near September levels while transaction trends improved, supporting payment providers with broad merchant exposure.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to see these trends as supportive for payment providers

theme_stances.key_argument: Essentials growth outpaced discretionary and is accelerating, which favors a non-discretionary spend portfolio.
theme_stances.evidence: continued strength in essentials remains supportive for CHYM
